paladin.detectEvil: A paladin can detect the presence of evil intent up to 60 feet away by concentrating on locating evil in a particular direction. They can do this as often as desired, but each attempt takes one round. This ability detects evil monsters and characters.
paladin.savebontext: Saving Throws. A paladin receives a +2 bonus to all saving throws.
paladin.immunityText: Disease immunity. A paladin is immune to all forms of disease. (Note that certain magical afflictions—lycanthropy and mummy rot—are curses and not diseases.)
paladin.layOnText: Lay on Hands. Once per day a Paladin can restores 2 hit points per experience level. They can heal themself or someone else
paladin.cureDisText: Cure Diseases. A paladin can cure diseases of all sorts (though not cursed afflictions such as lycanthropy). Once per week for each five levels of experience (once per week at levels 1 through 5, twice per week at levels 6 through 10, etc.).
paladin.protEvilText: Protection from Evil. A paladin is surrounded by an aura of protection with a 10-foot radius. Within this radius, all summoned and specifically evil creatures suffer a -1 penalty to their attack rolls, regardless of whom they attack. Creatures affected by this aura can spot its source easily, even if the paladin is disguised.
paladin.holyWeap: Holy Weapons. A paladin using a holy sword projects a circle of power 10 feet in diameter when the sword is unsheathed and held. This power dispels hostile magic of a level up to the paladin's experience level. (A holy sword is a very special weapon; if your paladin acquires one, the DM will explain its other powers.)
paladin.faithMount: Faithful Mount. A paladin may call for their war horse upon reaching 4th level, or anytime thereafter. This faithful steed need not be a horse; it may be whatever sort of creature is appropriate to the character (as decided by the DM). A paladin's war horse is a very special animal, bonded by fate to the warrior. The paladin does not really 'call' the animal, nor does the horse instantly appear in front of them. Rather, the character must find their war horse in some memorable way, most frequently by a specific quest.
paladin.languageSlots: Can use Language Slots from Intelligence for Nonweapon Proficiencies Slots

ranger.tracking: Tracking (Skill). You automatically gain the Tracking skill without expending a non-weapon proficiency.
ranger.survival: Survival (Skill). You automatically gain the Survival skill. The ranger is exceptionally skilled at surviving harsh conditions associated with his Primarv Terrain.
ranger.dualWield: Dual Wielding. A ranger may use two weapons simultaneously without the standard penalties if wearing Ring Mail or lighter armour. The following restrictions also apply; the main weapon is usable one handed, the second be smaller in size and weigh less than the main weapon
ranger.stealth: Stealth. You can also hide in shadows and move silently while wearing armour less than AC 7 or lower e.g. Ring Mail
ranger.speciesEnemy: Species Enemy. You have a particular enmity with a particular specied. Choose this before advancing to 2nd level. You gain +4 to hit when fighting this enemy and (Charisma) Reaction Penalty of -4 when seeing them.
ranger.animalEmpathy: Animal Empathy. Rangershave an innate understanding of animal behavior giving a limited ability to influence their emotions and manipulate their behavior. Animal saves vs Rods minus the Rangers modifier
ranger.nature: Nature Lore. All rangers have an inherent understanding of natural lore, encompassing a broad set of principles involving conservation, ecology, and natural order. Though not every ranger knows specific details about particular situations, all of them understand the general concepts at work.
ranger.languageSlots: Can use Language Slots from Intelligence for Nonweapon Proficiencies Slots

fighter.specialise: Fighters can double specialise in weapons. There may be house rules regarding how it's handled, ask the DM
fighter.languageSlots: Can use Language Slots from Intelligence for Nonweapon Proficiencies Slots

mage.spellBook: At 1st-level the spell book contains 3d4 1st-level spells. Read Magic and Detect Magic are required.
mage.languageSlots: Can use Language Slots from Intelligence for Nonweapon Proficiencies Slots

specialist wizard.spellBook: At 1st-level the spell book contains 3d4 1st-level spells. Read Magic and Detect Magic are required. 1 of the starting spells can be of the Specialist Wizard's specialty (1st level spell only) without making a learn spells roll

druid.saveBonText: +2 to all saving throws vs. fire or electrical attacks
druid.languageSlots: Can use Language Slots from Intelligence for Nonweapon Proficiencies Slots. All druids can speak a secret language in addition to any other tongues they know. Druids jealously guard this language; it is the one infallible method they have of recognizing each other.

Gains the ability to shapechange into a reptile, bird, or mammal up to three times per day. Each animal form (reptile, bird, or mammal) can be used only once per day. The size can vary from that of a bullfrog or small bird to as large as a black bear. Upon assuming a new form, the druid heals 10-60% (1d6 в 10%) of all damage he has suffered (round fractions down). The druid can only assume the form of a normal (real world) animal in its normal proportions, but by doing so he takes on all of that creature's characteristics—its movement rate and abilities, its Armor Class, number of attacks, and damage per attack.

thief.backstab: Backstab. A thief can strike for extra damage when attacking an opponent from behind. The thief must be able to see the target and be within 10 feet of it. The thief does not need to be hidden, but the target must not be aware of the thief's presence. The thief can backstab for 1d6 extra damage at 1st level, and this increases by 1d6 every three levels thereafter (2d6 at 4th level, 3d6 at 7th level, etc.).
thief.pickPockets: Pick Pockets. A thief can attempt to pick pockets once per round. The chance of success is based on the thief's level and the type of victim (see Pick Pockets Table). If successful, the thief steals a random item from the victim's inventory. The victim is unaware of the theft unless they succeed on a Perception check against the thief's Stealth skill.
thief.openLocks: Open Locks. A thief can attempt to open locks once per round. The chance of success is based on the thief's level and the complexity of the lock (see Open Locks Table). If successful, the lock is opened without triggering any traps that may be present.
thief.findRemoveTraps: Find/Remove Traps. A thief can attempt to find or remove traps once per round. The chance of success is based on the thief's level and the complexity of the trap (see Find/Remove Traps Table). If successful, the trap is either detected or disarmed without triggering it.
thief.moveSilently: Move Silently. A thief can attempt to move silently once per round. The chance of success is based on the thief's level and the environment (see Move Silently Table). If successful, the thief moves without making any noise that could alert nearby creatures.
thief.hideInShadows: Hide in Shadows. A thief can attempt to hide in shadows once per round. The chance of success is based on the thief's level and the lighting conditions (see Hide in Shadows Table). If successful, the thief becomes invisible while in shadows, making it difficult for enemies to detect them.
thief.detectNoise: Detect Noise. A thief can attempt to detect noise once per round. The chance of success is based on the thief's level and the distance of the noise (see Detect Noise Table). If successful, the thief can pinpoint the source of the noise within a certain radius.
thief.climbWalls: Climb Walls. A thief can attempt to climb walls once per round. The chance of success is based on the thief's level and the type of surface (see Climb Walls Table). If successful, the thief can climb vertical surfaces without falling.
thief.readLanguages: Read Languages. A thief can attempt to read languages once per round. The chance of success is based on the thief's level and the complexity of the language (see Read Languages Table). If successful, the thief can understand written text in a language they do not know, allowing them to decipher clues or read important documents.
